en: 9  Dreamland
zh: 9  梦幻乐园

en: During the second half of the twentieth century, economics established its claim to be the true political science. The idea of “the economy” provided a mode of seeing and a way of organizing the world that could diagnose a country’s fundamental condition, frame the terms of its public debate, picture its collective growth or decline, and propose remedies for its improvement, all in terms of what seemed a legible series of measurements, goals, and comparisons. In the closing decade of the century, after the collapse of state socialism in the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe, the authority of economic science seemed stronger than ever.

Employing the language and authority of neoclassical economics, the programs of economic reform and structural adjustment advocated in Washington by the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank, and the United States government could judge the condition of a nation and its collective well-being by simply measuring its monetary and fiscal balances.
zh: 20世纪下半叶，经济学确立了其作为真正政治科学的地位。“经济”这一观念提供了一种观察模式和组织世界的方式，它能诊断一个国家的根本状况，框定其公共辩论的用语，描绘其集体增长或衰退，并提出改善的补救办法——所有这一切都通过一系列看似清晰可读的衡量指标、目标和比较来表述。在该世纪最后十年，苏联和东欧国家社会主义崩溃之后，经济科学的权威似乎比以往任何时候都更强大。
国际货币基金组织（IMF）、世界银行和美国政府在华盛顿倡导的经济改革与结构调整计划，运用新古典经济学的语言和权威，只需衡量一国的货币和财政收支，就能评判该国的状况及其集体福祉。

en: In Egypt, according to these ways of thinking, the 1990s was a decade of remarkable success that vindicated the principles of neoliberalism. After the government agreed to an IMF reform program, fiscal and monetary discipline brought the inflation rate below 5 percent and reduced the budget deficit from 15 percent of the country’s gross domestic product (GDP) to less than 3 percent and for some years less than 1 percent, among the lowest levels in the world. The economy was said to be growing at more than 5 percent a year, and a revitalized private capitalism now accounted for two-thirds of domestic investment. The value of the Egyptian pound was pegged to the U.S. dollar, supported by hard currency reserves of more than $18 billion. These half a dozen financial figures, repeated countless times in government newspapers and television bulletins and in publications of the IMF, constituted the picture of the “remarkable turnaround in Egypt’s macroeconomic fortunes” in the final years of the century.
zh: 按照这些思路，在埃及，1990年代是一个非凡成功的十年，证明了新自由主义原则的正确。政府同意IMF改革计划后，财政和货币纪律使通胀率降至5%以下，并把预算赤字从该国国内生产总值（GDP）的15%降至3%以下，有些年份甚至低于1%，属于世界最低水平之列。据称经济以每年5%以上的速度增长，重振的私人资本主义现在占国内投资的三分之二。埃及镑币值盯住美元，得到180多亿美元硬通货储备的支撑。这六七个财政数字在政府报纸、电视新闻和IMF出版物中被无数次重复，构成了该世纪最后几年“埃及宏观经济命运非凡好转”的图景。

en: Yet if one looked beyond the official figures, even elsewhere in the same newspapers and television programs, other developments seemed to contradict this view. Accompanying the picture of monetary control and fiscal discipline was a contrasting image of uncontrolled expansion and limitless dreams. The most dramatic example was the country’s rapidly expanding capital city. While government budgets were contracting, Cairo was exploding. “Dreamland,” the TV commercials for the most ambitious of the new developments promised, “is the world’s first electronic city.” Buyers were invited to sign up now for luxury fiber optic–wired villas, as the shopping malls and theme park, golf course and polo grounds, rose out of the desert west of the Giza pyramids—but only minutes from central Cairo on the newly built ring road. Or one could take the ring road the other way, east of the Muqattam Hills, to the desert of “New Cairo,” where speculators were marketing apartment blocks to expatriate workers saving for their futures in the Gulf. “Sign now for a future value beyond any dreams,” prospective buyers were told, “ . . . Before it is too late.” Purchasers could start payments immediately (no deposit was required) at agencies in Jeddah and Dubai. “No factories, no pollution, no problems” was the advertisement’s promise, accompanied by the developer’s slogan, “The Egypt of My Desires.”

The development tracts stretched out across the fields and deserts around Greater Cairo represented the largest real estate explosion Egypt had ever seen. Within the second half of the 1990s the area of its capital city seemed to have doubled—but a symptom of the way it happened was that there were no maps available that might confirm this.
zh: 然而，如果越过官方数字，哪怕只看同一批报纸和电视节目中的其他内容，其他发展似乎都与这一看法相矛盾。与货币控制和财政纪律的图景相伴的，是一幅截然相反的失控扩张和无边梦想的图像。最戏剧性的例子是该国迅速扩张的首都。政府预算在收缩，开罗却在爆炸式扩张。最雄心勃勃的新开发项目的电视广告承诺：“梦幻乐园是全世界第一座电子城市。”广告邀请买家现在签约购买光纤布线的高级别墅；购物中心、主题公园、高尔夫球场和马球场正从吉萨金字塔以西的沙漠中拔地而起——但借助新建的环城公路，距开罗市中心只有几分钟车程。或者沿环城公路驶向另一方向，到穆卡塔姆山以东的“新开罗”沙漠，投机者正向在海湾为未来攒钱的外派劳工推销公寓楼。潜在买家被告知：“现在就签约，锁定超越任何梦想的未来价值……趁还来得及。”买家可以在吉达和迪拜的代理处立即开始付款（无需定金）。广告承诺“没有工厂，没有污染，没有问题”，并附有开发商的标语：“我渴望的埃及”。
在大开罗周边的田野和沙漠上铺开的开发地块，代表着埃及前所未见的最大规模房地产爆炸。1990年代后半期，首都的面积似乎翻了一番——但这一发生方式的一个症状是，竟然找不到可以证实这一点的地图。

en: The exuberance of the private developers was matched by the state. While speculative builders were doubling the size of Cairo, the government was proposing to duplicate the Nile River. In October 1996 President Mubarak announced the revival of plans from the 1950s to construct a parallel valley by pumping water out of the lake behind the Aswan High Dam in the south into a canal running northwards that would eventually irrigate two million acres of the Western Desert.

Unable to persuade the World Bank or commercial investors that the Toshka scheme, as it was known, was feasible, the government proceeded with building the pumping station and an initial seventy kilometers of the canal, broadcasting daily television pictures of Caterpillar earth movers toiling in the desert.

It allocated the first 100,000 acres of future farmland to a man described as the world’s second-richest person, the Saudi financier Prince al-Walid bin Talal, whose Kingdom Agricultural Development Company appointed a California agribusiness, Sun World, to develop and manage what would become the world’s single largest farm, consuming by itself 1 percent of the waters of the Nile.
zh: 私人开发商的狂热与国家不相上下。投机建筑商在使开罗面积翻倍的同时，政府提议复制尼罗河。1996年10月，穆巴拉克总统宣布重启1950年代的各项计划：从南方阿斯旺大坝后的湖泊抽水，注入一条向北延伸的运河，最终灌溉西部沙漠两百万费丹土地。
政府未能说服世界银行或商业投资者相信这个被称为托什卡的方案可行，却继续建设泵站和最初七十公里的运河，每天播放卡特彼勒土方机械在沙漠中辛苦作业的电视画面。
它把未来农田的头10万费丹分配给一名被称为世界第二富豪的人——沙特金融家瓦利德·本·塔拉勒亲王。他的王国农业发展公司任命加州农业综合企业太阳世界（Sun World）来开发和管理这座将成为世界最大单一农场的农场，仅它一家就要消耗尼罗河水量的1%。

en: Sun World specialized in growing grapes and other table fruits on irrigated lands and owned the global patents of more than fifty commercial varieties of fruit cultivar. The company was to invest no money of its own in the Toshka project, however, or even pay its own management expenses. In the excitement of the government’s announcement that the project had found an American partner, the reason for this went unnoticed: Sun World had no money. The corporation was another failure of the U.S. farm industry and had recently gone bankrupt. A second struggling California agribusiness, Cadiz, had taken over Sun World, planning to pay off its debts by transforming it from a company producing crops into a marketing business that would sell its patents and trademarks, including its flagship brand, Superior SeedlessTM grapes, around the world. Unable to make money growing and selling grapes, the company would sell the names of grapes instead. The company’s global patents would guarantee it a future payment on every grape, peach, plum, and nectarine that Egyptian farmers laboring in the Western Desert might one day grow.

The government agreed to provide 20 percent of the farm’s capital and granted it the twenty-year tax holiday enjoyed by large investors, but the government and Prince al-Walid were still looking for other private sector partners willing to put up money for the project.
zh: 太阳世界专长于在灌溉土地上种植葡萄和其他鲜食水果，并拥有五十多个商业水果品种的全球专利。然而，该公司不会在托什卡项目中投入自己的任何资金，甚至不支付自己的管理开销。政府兴奋地宣布该项目找到了一个美国合作伙伴，却没有注意到这背后的原因：太阳世界没有钱。这家公司是美国农业的又一次失败，最近刚刚破产。另一家挣扎求生的加州农业综合企业卡迪斯（Cadiz）接管了太阳世界，计划把它从生产作物的公司转变为销售其专利和商标的营销企业，以此偿还债务，包括在世界各地销售其旗舰品牌“超级无籽”（Superior Seedless™）葡萄。既然种葡萄、卖葡萄赚不到钱，公司就改为卖葡萄的名字。该公司的全球专利将保证：埃及农民有朝一日在西部沙漠辛勤种出的每一颗葡萄、桃子、李子和油桃，都要向它支付一笔款项。
政府同意提供农场资本的20%，并给予其大型投资者享有的二十年免税期，但政府和瓦利德亲王仍在寻找其他愿意为该项目出资的私营部门合作伙伴。

en: In the meantime the state was subsidizing the urban property developers as well, selling public land cheaply and building the required expressways and Nile bridges in good time. The state was also involved directly, as a property developer. Down the road from Dreamland, adjacent to a U.S.- managed speculative development named Beverly Hills, the Radio and Television Union, a commercial arm of the Ministry of Information, was building a theme park and filmmaking facility called Media Production City, at thirty-five million square meters billed as the world’s biggest media complex outside Hollywood.

And the largest builder of Cairo’s new neighborhoods, far bigger than the builders of Dreamland or Beverly Hills, was the Ministry of Defense. Military contractors were throwing up thousands of acres of apartments on the city’s eastern perimeter to create a new suburbia for the officer class.
zh: 与此同时，国家也在补贴城市房地产开发商，低价出售公共土地，并及时修建所需的快速路和尼罗河桥梁。国家还作为房地产开发商直接参与其中。在梦幻乐园往下不远、紧邻一个由美国管理的名为“比弗利山庄”的投机开发项目之处，新闻部的商业机构广播电视联盟正在建设一座名为“媒体制作城”的主题公园和影视制作设施，占地三千五百万平方米，号称好莱坞以外世界最大的媒体综合体。
而开罗新城区最大的建设者，远比梦幻乐园或比弗利山庄的开发商更大，是国防部。军方承包商在城市东郊迅速建起数千费丹的公寓，为军官阶层打造一个新的郊区世界。

en: If one’s first reaction was amazement at the scale and speed of these developments, one soon began to wonder about the contradictions. The IMF and Ministry of the Economy spoke calmly of financial discipline and sustainable economic growth, but made no mention of the frenzied explosion of the capital city or the ecologically disastrous valley-making schemes in the desert.

The role of the state in subsidizing this speculative investment, and the networks linking speculators, bankers, and state officials, went unexamined. A further problem was that financial stabilization and structural adjustment were intended to generate an export boom, not a building boom. Egypt was to prosper by selling fruits and vegetables to Europe and the Gulf, not paving over its fields to build ring roads. But real estate had now replaced agriculture as the country’s third-largest nonoil investment sector, after manufacturing and tourism.
Indeed it may have become the largest nonoil sector, since most tourism investment went into building hotels and vacation homes, another form of real estate.
zh: 如果一个人的第一反应是对这些发展的规模和速度感到惊讶，那么他很快就会开始思考其中的矛盾。IMF和经济部平静地谈论财政纪律和可持续经济增长，却只字不提首都的疯狂扩张或沙漠中生态灾难性的造谷计划。
国家在补贴这种投机投资中所扮演的角色，以及把投机者、银行家和政府官员联系起来的网络，都未受到审视。还有一个问题：金融稳定和结构调整本应带来出口繁荣，而不是建筑繁荣。埃及本应通过向欧洲和海湾出售水果蔬菜而繁荣，而不是把田地铺平来修环城公路。但房地产现在已经取代农业，成为该国第三大非石油投资部门，仅次于制造业和旅游业。
事实上，它可能已成为最大的非石油部门，因为大部分旅游投资都用于建造旅馆和度假住宅——另一种形式的房地产。

en: The reforms were supposed to open Egypt to trade with the global market. In fact they had the opposite effect. The country’s openness index, which measures the value of exports and imports of goods and services as a proportion of GDP, collapsed from 88 percent in 1985 to 47 percent in 1996–97. In the same period Egypt’s share of world exports also dropped by more than half.

The value of nonoil exports actually shrank in 1995–96, then shrank again in 1996–97, leaving the country dependent on petroleum products for 52 percent of its export income. By the end of 1998 the situation was still worse, as the collapse of world petroleum prices forced Egypt briefly to halt its oil exports.

In 1998–99 the U.S. government quietly set about rebuilding the OPEC oil cartel, it was reported, holding secret negotiations with Iran, Saudi Arabia, and Venezuela in which it traded political concessions for promises to cut production. The negotiations were a success, doubling the price of oil again within six months.
But this unpublicized state management of world trade was too late to solve Egypt’s new balance of payments crisis and the repeated shortages of foreign currency.
zh: 改革本应使埃及向全球市场贸易开放。事实上，效果恰恰相反。该国的开放度指数——以商品和服务进出口值占GDP的比例衡量——从1985年的88%暴跌至1996—97年的47%。同一时期，埃及在世界出口中的份额也下降了一半以上。
非石油出口值在1995—96年实际萎缩，1996—97年再次萎缩，使该国出口收入的52%依赖石油产品。到1998年底情况更糟，世界油价崩溃迫使埃及一度停止石油出口。
据报道，1998—99年美国政府悄悄着手重建欧佩克石油卡特尔，与伊朗、沙特阿拉伯和委内瑞拉进行秘密谈判，以政治让步换取减产承诺。谈判成功了，六个月内油价再次翻倍。
但这种未加宣扬的国家对世界贸易的管理，已来不及解决埃及新的国际收支危机和反复出现的外汇短缺。

en: The most visible element in Egypt’s picture of success, the stabilization of the value of its money, owed nothing to the power of the market. It came about because the government was now better able to insulate the local currency against speculative exchanges of international finance. In other words, the reforms depended not on freer trade and greater global integration but on reorganizing local protection against an international market in the buying and selling of money. The protection of the currency relied upon the often announced $18 billion of foreign reserves, a figure that alone came to symbolize the strength of the economy. The symbolism was so important that the government was unwilling actually to spend its reserves in defense of the currency. When exports fell even further and the trade balance worsened again in 1998–99, it resorted to a series of ingenious measures to impede the flow of imports and thus the exodus of hard currency, insulating the country further against the global market.
zh: 埃及成功图景中最显眼的要素——货币价值的稳定——与市场力量毫无关系。它之所以实现，是因为政府现在更有能力使本国货币免受国际金融投机交易的影响。换言之，改革所依赖的不是更自由的贸易和更大的全球一体化，而是重新组织本地保护，以抵御一个买卖货币的国际市场。货币保护依赖于经常被宣布的180亿美元外汇储备——仅这个数字本身就象征着经济实力。这种象征意义如此重要，以至于政府不愿真正动用储备来捍卫货币。1998—99年出口进一步下降、贸易收支再度恶化时，它采取了一系列巧妙措施来阻碍进口流入，从而阻止硬通货外流，使该国进一步与世界市场隔绝。

en: How does one account for developments that seem so at odds with official representations? The conventional story was that by 1990 the Egyptian economy was in crisis, no longer able to support loss-making public industries, an overvalued currency, profligate government spending, an inflationary printing of money to cover the budget gap, and astronomical levels of foreign debt.

After fifteen years of foot dragging and partial reforms, including the agricultural price reforms discussed in chapter 8, in 1990–91 the government was forced to adopt an IMF stabilization plan that allowed the currency to collapse against the dollar, decreased the government budget, tightened the supply of money, and cut back subsidies to public sector enterprises, which the government reorganized into holding companies that were to privatize them or shut them down. These “prudent” fiscal policies were implemented more drastically than even the IMF had demanded, achieving a drop in the government deficit that the IMF called “virtually unparalleled in recent years.”
zh: 如何解释那些似乎与官方表述如此不符的发展？通常的说法是，到1990年埃及经济已陷入危机，再也无法支撑亏损的公有产业、高估的货币、挥霍无度的政府开支、为弥补预算缺口而引发通胀的印钞，以及天文数字的外债。
在十五年的拖延和部分改革（包括第8章讨论的农业价格改革）之后，政府于1990—91年被迫采纳IMF稳定计划：让货币对美元大幅贬值，削减政府预算，收紧货币供应，并削减对公共部门企业的补贴；政府把这些企业重组为控股公司，由控股公司将其私有化或关闭。这些“审慎”的财政政策执行得比IMF的要求还要猛烈，使政府赤字下降，IMF称之为“近年来几乎无与伦比”。

en: Some accounts were willing to admit that the story had more elements than this simple tale of a prodigal state starting a new life of prudence. They may have added, for example, that among the most profligate of the government’s expenditures was the purchase of military equipment, much of it supplied and subsidized by the United States—as part of Washington’s own system of subsidies to U.S. military industries. An impending default on these military debts, causing an automatic suspension of U.S. aid, helped trigger the collapse in 1990. (Egypt had begun to default as early as 1983, but as we know, for several years the U.S. government illegally diverted its own funds to pay off Egypt’s military loans.)

Some accounts may also have acknowledged that the crisis was brought on not just by a spendthrift state but by wider disruptions beyond its control, in particular the decline after 1985 in the price of oil (the largest source of government revenue); the halting of secret U.S. purchases of Egyptian weapons for Washington’s covert war against Afghanistan (1979–89); and the decrease in workers’ remittances, arms exports to Iraq, and other foreign income caused by the 1990–91 Gulf conflict.

The Iraq crisis enabled the United States and other creditors in Europe and the Gulf to write off almost half Egypt’s external debt, cutting it from U.S.$53 billion in 1988 to $28 billion. The savings on interest payments, amounting to $15.5 billion by 1996–97, accounted for all of the increase in currency reserves.
So the largest single contribution to Egypt’s fiscal turnaround resulted from a political decision of the United States and its allies. It had nothing to do with neoliberalism.
zh: 有些叙述愿意承认，这个故事包含的要素不止“浪子国家开始审慎新生活”这么简单。例如，它们可能补充说，政府最挥霍的开支之一是购买军事装备，其中许多由美国供应和补贴——这是华盛顿补贴美国军工产业自身体系的一部分。这些军事债务即将违约，会连带自动中止美国援助，从而促成了1990年的崩溃。（埃及早在1983年就开始违约，但如我们所见，美国政府多年来非法挪用自身资金替埃及偿还军事贷款。）
有些叙述可能还承认，危机的起因不只是国家挥霍，还有它无法控制的更广泛冲击，尤其是1985年后油价下跌（政府收入的最大来源）、美国为华盛顿对阿富汗的秘密战争（1979—89）而秘密购买埃及武器的中止，以及1990—91年海湾冲突造成的工人汇款、对伊拉克武器出口和其他外汇收入的减少。
伊拉克危机使美国以及欧洲和海湾的其他债权国得以勾销埃及近一半外债，从1988年的530亿美元降至280亿美元。到1996—97年，利息支付的节省额达到155亿美元，构成了外汇储备的全部增量。
因此，对埃及财政好转贡献最大的单一因素，是美国及其盟友的政治决定。它与新自由主义毫无关系。

en: Furthermore, an important part of government revenue in Egypt in the 1990s came not from taxing productive activities but from the rent derived from public resources. About one-third came from two state-owned enterprises, the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation and the Suez Canal Authority. The revenues of these enterprises were earned in U.S. dollars, so the one-third devaluation of the Egyptian pound against the dollar increased their value by 50 percent. This increase contributed the bulk of the growth in government revenues in the stabilization period. Again, the fiscal magic was little connected with free-market principles. In this case it owed more to the extensive ownership of resources by the state.
zh: 此外，1990年代埃及政府收入的重要部分并非来自对生产活动征税，而是来自公共资源所得的地租。约三分之一来自两家国有企业：埃及石油总公司和苏伊士运河管理局。这些企业的收入以美元计，因此埃及镑对美元贬值三分之一使其价值增加了50%。这一增长构成了稳定时期政府收入增长的大部分。同样，这种财政魔术与自由市场原则几乎无关。在这个案例中，它更多归因于国家对资源的广泛所有权。

en: Beyond all this there was another, still more complex story, one that exceeded the terms of official accounts and was pushed aside into footnotes. The crisis of 1990–91 was not just a problem of public enterprises losing money or a profligate government overspending. It was also a problem of the so-called private sector and the chaos brought on by deregulated international flows of speculative finance. The financial reforms that followed were not so much an elimination of state support, as the official version of events portrayed things, but more a change in who received it. The “free market” program in Egypt was better seen as a multilayered political readjustment of rents, subsidies, and the control of resources. In the following pages I retrieve this story from the footnotes. The second half of the chapter then considers what its burial there can tell us about the larger questions these events pose: How should we understand the relationship between the expertise of economics and the object we call the economy? What combination of understandings and silences, forces and desires, makes possible the economy? Why do these elements at the same time render the making of the economy incomplete?
zh: 在这一切之外，还有一个更为复杂的故事，它超出了官方叙述的范围，被推到脚注里。1990—91年的危机不只是公有企业亏损或政府挥霍超支的问题。它也是所谓私营部门的问题，以及放松管制的国际投机金融流动所带来的混乱。随后的金融改革，与其像官方版本所描述的那样取消了国家支持，不如说是改变了谁获得支持。埃及的“自由市场”计划，更应被看作对地租、补贴和资源控制进行的多层次政治调整。在接下来的篇幅中，我将从脚注中打捞这个故事。本章后半部分随后将探讨：它被埋进脚注这一事实，能就这些事件提出的更大问题告诉我们什么：我们应该如何理解经济学专业知识与我们称为经济的对象之间的关系？哪些理解与沉默、力量与欲望的组合使经济成为可能？为什么这些要素同时使经济的生成变得不完整？

en: First, it was not in fact the case that public sector enterprises were losing money. In 1989–90, on the eve of the reforms, 260 out of 314 nonfinancial state-owned enterprises were profitable and only 54 were suffering losses. While the latter lost E£300 million ($110 million), the profitable companies made after-tax profits of E£1.5 billion (about $550 million).

At the center of concern in 1990–91 was a crisis not of state-owned industry but of the financial sector, which brought the country’s banking system close to collapse. Since 1974 the number of banks had increased from seven to ninety-eight, as commercial banks sprang up to finance the imports and investments of the oil-boom years. The four large state-owned banks made loans mostly to public sector enterprises. It was estimated that at least 30 percent of these loans were nonperforming.
But the state banks were also part owners of the private sector banks, enabling them to channel public funds toward a small group of wealthy and well-connected entrepreneurs.
These large private sector borrowers were also in trouble.
zh: 首先，公共部门企业实际上并没有亏损。1989—90年，即改革前夕，314家非金融国有企业中有260家盈利，只有54家亏损。后者亏损3亿埃镑（1.1亿美元），而盈利企业税后利润达15亿埃镑（约5.5亿美元）。
1990—91年关注的核心不是国有工业的危机，而是金融部门的危机，它使该国银行体系濒临崩溃。自1974年以来，银行数量从七家增加到九十八家，商业银行纷纷涌现，为石油繁荣年代的进口和投资提供融资。四大国有银行主要向公共部门企业放贷。据估计，其中至少30%是坏账。
但国有银行也是私营银行的股东，使它们能把公共资金输送给一小群富有且人脉广泛的企业家。
这些私营部门的大借款人同样陷入了困境。

en: By 1989 26 percent of private and investment loans were in default, more than half of them belonging to just 3 percent of defaulters. Many of the big debtors were able to delay legal action, and others fled the country to avoid the courts.

The largest default came in July 1991, when the London-based Bank of Credit and Commerce International collapsed. (The biggest bank ever to collapse, BCCI had been the leading global finance house for the funding of secret wars, helping the CIA launder payments for U.S. wars in the 1980s against Nicaragua and Afghanistan.) Depositors in BCCI’s Egyptian subsidiary were protected by an informal insurance scheme among Egyptian banks, which had to contribute 0.5 percent of their deposits and share the cost of a E£1 billion interest-free loan to make up the missing funds.
zh: 到1989年，26%的私人贷款和投资贷款已经违约，其中一半以上仅属于3%的违约者。许多大债务人得以拖延法律诉讼，另一些人则逃往国外以躲避法院。
最大的违约发生在1991年7月，总部位于伦敦的国际信贷商业银行（BCCI）倒闭。（BCCI是有史以来倒闭的最大银行，曾是资助秘密战争的主要全球金融机构，帮助中央情报局为美国1980年代对尼加拉瓜和阿富汗的战争洗钱。）BCCI埃及子公司的存款人受到埃及银行之间一项非正式保险计划的保护：各银行须缴纳其存款的0.5%，并分摊一笔10亿埃镑无息贷款的成本，以弥补缺失的资金。

en: These difficulties reflected the problems of a state in which public interests, as we will see, were increasingly entwined with the projects of a wellconnected group of financiers and entrepreneurs, whose actions it was unable to discipline.

As with the 1997–99 global financial crisis, however, the problem of public resources overflowing into private networks cannot be separated from the difficulties caused by global speculation, especially currency trading.

Following the abandoning of international currency controls in 1980, pioneered by the United States and Canada, daily global foreign exchange turnover increased from $82.5 billion in 1980 to $270 billion in 1986 and $590 billion in 1989 (by 1995 it was to reach $1.23 trillion).
The growth of private and institutional speculation in national currencies overwhelmed the attempts of governments to manage their currencies according to local needs.
zh: 这些困难反映了一个国家的问题：正如我们将看到的，公共利益日益与一群人脉广泛的金融家和企业家的事业缠绕在一起，而国家无法约束他们的行为。
然而，同1997—99年全球金融危机一样，公共资源溢出到私人网络的问题，与全球投机——尤其是货币交易——造成的困难无法分开。
1980年美国和加拿大率先放弃国际货币管制之后，全球每日外汇交易额从1980年的825亿美元增至1986年的2700亿美元和1989年的5900亿美元（到1995年将达到1.23万亿美元）。
私人和机构对国家货币的投机增长，压倒了政府按本地需要管理本国货币的努力。

en: In Egypt global deregulation coincided with a sudden increase in private foreign currency transfers, as expatriate workers sent home earnings from the Gulf. More than one hundred unregulated money management firms were formed to transfer and invest such funds, five or six of them growing very large.

These Islamic investment companies (so called because they appealed to depositors by describing the dividend they paid as a profit share rather than an interest payment) invested successfully in currency speculation, later diversifying into local tourism, real estate, manufacturing, and commodity dealing, and paid returns that kept ahead of inflation. The public and private sector commercial banks, subject to high reserve requirements and low official interest rates (essential to the government financing of industry), could not compete and were increasingly starved of hard currency. The financial system was in crisis.
zh: 在埃及，全球放松管制恰逢私人外汇转移突然增加，因为外派劳工从海湾寄回收入。一百多家不受监管的资金管理公司成立，专门转移和投资这些资金，其中五六家发展得非常大。
这些伊斯兰投资公司（之所以这样称呼，是因为它们把支付的红利说成分红而非利息，以此吸引储户）成功投资于货币投机，后来扩展到本地旅游、房地产、制造业和商品交易，支付的回报率超过通胀。公共和私营部门的商业银行受制于高准备金要求和低官方利率（这对政府为工业融资至关重要），无法竞争，日益缺乏硬通货。金融体系陷入危机。

en: In 1988–89 the bankers finally persuaded the government to eliminate the investment companies. It passed a law that suspended their operations for up to a year, then closed down those it found insolvent (or in many cases made insolvent) and forced the remainder to reorganize as joint-stock companies and deposit their liquid assets in the banks. The measure protected the banks and their well-connected clients but provoked a general financial depression from which neither the banks nor the national currency could recover.
zh: 1988—89年，银行家们终于说服政府取缔这些投资公司。政府通过一项法律，暂停这些公司运营最长一年，随后关闭被认定资不抵债的公司（在许多情况下是使它们资不抵债），并迫使其余公司重组为股份公司，将其流动资产存入银行。这项措施保护了银行及其人脉广泛的客户，却引发了一场普遍的金融萧条，银行和本国货币都未能从中恢复。

en: In response to the financial crisis, the centerpiece of the 1990–91 reforms was an effort to rescue the country’s banks. After allowing the currency to collapse and cutting public investment projects, the government transferred to the banks funds worth 5.5 percent of GDP, in the form of treasury bills.

To give an idea of the scale of this subsidy, in the United States during the same period the government paid for the rescue of the savings and loan industry, which had collapsed following financial deregulation, transferring a sum that amounted to about 3 percent of GDP over ten years. The Egyptian payment was almost twice as large in relation to GDP and occurred in a single year. Moreover, the government declared the banks’ income from these funds to be tax free, a fiscal subsidy amounting to a further 10 percent of GDP by 1996–97. In 1998 the government attempted to end the subsidy by reintroducing the taxing of bank profits, but the bankers thwarted the implementation of the law.
The banks became highly profitable, enjoying rates of return on equity of 20 percent or more. All of these profits were accounted for by the income from the government rescue.
zh: 为应对金融危机，1990—91年改革的核心是努力拯救该国银行。在任由货币崩溃并削减公共投资项目之后，政府以国库券形式向银行转移了相当于GDP 5.5%的资金。
为说明这笔补贴的规模：同一时期，美国政府为拯救在金融放松管制后崩溃的储贷业所转移的资金，十年间约为GDP的3%。埃及的支付相对于GDP几乎翻倍，而且在一年内完成。此外，政府宣布银行从这些资金获得的收入免税，到1996—97年这笔财政补贴又相当于GDP的10%。1998年政府试图通过重新对银行利润征税来终止补贴，但银行家们阻挠了该法的实施。
银行变得利润丰厚，股本回报率达到20%或更高。所有这些利润都来自政府救助的收入。

en: A further support to the banking sector came when the government tightened the supply of money to raise interest rates, pushing them initially as high as 14 percent above international market levels. Nonmarket interest rates brought in a flood of speculative capital from abroad. This was quickly taken to indicate the success of neoliberal discipline and market orthodoxy. It was nothing of the sort. The money consisted of highly volatile investment funds chasing interest income whose attractiveness was due not to “market fundamentals” but state intervention. After two years interest rates were brought down and the miniboom passed.
zh: 政府对银行部门的进一步支持，是收紧货币供应以提高利率，起初把利率推高至国际市场水平以上14个百分点。非市场利率引来大量海外投机资本。这很快被视为新自由主义纪律和市场正统成功的标志。事实并非如此。这些资金是追逐利息收入的高度易变投资基金，其吸引力并非来自“市场基本面”，而是来自国家干预。两年后利率下调，小型繁荣随之结束。

en: In 1996–97 the government manufactured another miniboom by announcing an aggressive program of privatization. It began to sell shares in state-owned enterprises on the Cairo stock market, which it had reorganized to exclude small brokers and eliminate taxes on profits.

By June 1997 the government’s income from the privatization sales amounted to E£5.2 billion ($1.5 billion). It used 40 percent of this income to provide further support to the banking sector by paying off bad debts. In May 1998 the IMF praised Egypt’s “remarkable” privatization program, ranking it fourth in the world (after Hungary, Malaysia, and the Czech Republic) in terms of privatization income as a share of GDP.
zh: 1996—97年，政府宣布一项激进的私有化计划，制造了又一场小型繁荣。它开始通过开罗股市出售国有企业股票，并已对股市进行重组，以排除小经纪人、取消利润税。
到1997年6月，政府的私有化销售收入达到52亿埃镑（15亿美元）。它把其中40%的收入用于清偿坏账，以进一步支持银行部门。1998年5月，IMF称赞埃及的私有化计划“成绩斐然”，按私有化收入占GDP的比例排名世界第四（仅次于匈牙利、马来西亚和捷克共和国）。

en: The sell-off fattened the banks and the government budget and fueled a short-lived stock market boom. But its outcome was not a switch from state-run enterprise to a reborn private sector. The conventional distinction between a private and a public sector, used by the government and the IMF, was too simple to capture the range of political and economic relations involved.

Many of the largest government-owned enterprises, such as Arab Contractors, the country’s largest construction firm, and Eastern Tobacco, the cigarette-manufacturing monopoly, had their own “private sector” subsidiaries or joint ventures, typically run by members of the same family managing the public sector parent.

The state banks were part owners of private sector banks, as we saw, and of other nonstate enterprises. A large number of government ministers and other senior officials, together with their spouses, siblings, and offspring, were partners or principal investors in many of the largest so-called private sector ventures.
zh: 出售国有资产养肥了银行和政府预算，并助长了短暂的股市繁荣。但其结果并不是从国有企业转向一个新生的私营部门。政府和IMF所用的公私部门传统区分过于简单，无法把握其中涉及的政治和经济关系范围。
许多最大的政府所有企业，如该国最大的建筑公司阿拉伯承包商和卷烟生产垄断企业东方烟草，都有自己的“私营部门”子公司或合资企业，通常由管理公共部门母公司的同一家族成员经营。
如我们所见，国有银行是私营银行的股东，也是其他非国有企业的股东。大量政府部长和其他高级官员，连同他们的配偶、兄弟姐妹和子女，是许多最大的所谓私营部门企业的合伙人或主要投资者。

en: In addition, the reorganization of state enterprises into corporate entities under the control of public holding companies further complicated the distinction between the public and private sectors. By June 30, 1999, the government had sold shares in 124 of its 314 nonfinancial public enterprises. However, it fully divested only a handful. The holding companies remained the largest shareholder in many, and the state managers continued to control others though employee shareholder associations.
The press was full of stories of phony privatizations, such as the December 1997 sale of al-Nasr Casting, which in fact had been sold to the public sector banks.
(A year later state officials forced the chairman of the stock exchange to resign after he tried to improve its surveillance of company finances and share trading.)

The state holding companies also set up new private sector subsidiaries, such as al-Ahram Cement, which was created by the state-owned cement companies and began to bid for shares in other cement companies the government was “privatizing.”
And many government ministries, with the support of public sector banks, began to launch new profit-making ventures, typified by the vast Media Production City project of the Ministry of Information.
zh: 此外，把国有企业重组为由公共控股公司控制的公司实体，进一步混淆了公私部门之间的区分。到1999年6月30日，政府已出售其314家非金融公共企业中的124家的股份。然而，它只在少数几家中完全撤资。控股公司仍是许多企业的最大股东，国家管理者还继续通过员工持股协会控制其他企业。
报纸上充斥着虚假私有化的报道，例如1997年12月出售的纳斯尔铸造公司，实际上被卖给了公共部门银行。
（一年后，因证券交易所主席试图加强对公司财务和股票交易的监管，国家官员迫使他辞职。）
国有控股公司还设立了新的私营部门子公司，例如由国有水泥公司创建的阿赫拉姆水泥公司，它开始竞购政府正在“私有化”的其他水泥公司的股份。
许多政府部门在公共部门银行的支持下开始推出新的营利性项目，新闻部庞大的媒体制作城项目就是典型。

en: The IMF’s confident report that Egypt ranked fourth in the world in privatization missed the complexity of these rearrangements and the multiple forms of ownership, interconnection, and power relationship involved. As David Stark argues in a study of Eastern Europe, by focusing on the enterprise as a unit and simply tallying the number and value of those moved from public to private ownership, orthodox accounts are unable to grasp the multiple methods of control, or the importance of the networks that combined them.

The blurred boundaries between “public” ownership and “private” had always offered ambiguities for state officials, enterprise managers, and other insiders to exploit to their own advantage. Structural adjustment offered opportunities for further combinations and new ambiguities. The economic reform was a complicated readjustment of the networks connecting and combining a variety of property assets, legal powers, information sources, and income flows.
zh: IMF自信地报告埃及的私有化排名世界第四，却忽视了这些重组的复杂性，以及其中涉及的所有权、相互联系和权力关系的多种形式。正如大卫·斯塔克在一项关于东欧的研究中所论证的，正统叙述以企业为单位，仅仅统计从公有转为私有的企业数目和价值，无法把握多种控制方法，也无法把握把这些方法结合起来的网络的重要性。
“公有”与“私有”之间模糊的界限，一直为国家官员、企业管理者和其他内部人提供可资利用以谋私利的含糊空间。结构调整为进一步的组合和新的含糊提供了机会。经济改革是对连接并结合各种财产资产、法律权力、信息来源和收入流的网络进行的复杂调整。

en: The stock market boom lasted less than eighteen months, with the EFG index of large capitalization companies reaching a peak in September 1997 then losing one-third of its value over the following twelve months.

As the stock market slid the government halted the sell-offs, suspending most privatizations after the summer of 1998 and stalling on an IMF demand to begin privatizing the financial sector. Instead, to stem the collapse of the market, the government used its financial institutions to invest public funds. Between December 1997 and October 1998 the large state-owned banks and insurance companies and the state pension fund pumped at least E£2 billion ($600 million) into the market, suffering large losses.

In the process the state reacquired shares in most of the companies it had recently claimed to be privatizing—further complicating the simple story of private capital replacing public ownership. The market recovered briefly in the winter of 1998–99, when the financial crises in East Asia, Brazil, and Russia made Egypt appear, thanks to its state-subsidized banking system, one of the few safe havens for international speculative funds, but after February 1999 the decline resumed. By the following summer the market was so flat that a single stock, the country’s newly privatized mobile phone monopoly, MobiNil, was regularly accounting for more than 50 percent of daily trading, and often up to 70 percent.
zh: 股市繁荣持续不到十八个月，EFG大盘股指数在1997年9月达到顶峰，随后十二个月里损失了三分之一的价值。
随着股市下滑，政府停止出售，1998年夏之后暂停了大部分私有化，并拖延IMF提出的开始私有化金融部门的要求。相反，为阻止市场崩溃，政府利用其金融机构投资公共资金。1997年12月至1998年10月间，大型国有银行、保险公司和国家养老基金向市场注入至少20亿埃镑（6亿美元），蒙受巨大损失。

在此过程中，国家重新获得了它最近声称要私有化的大多数公司的股份——使私人资本取代公有制的简单故事更加复杂。1998—99年冬天股市短暂回升：东亚、巴西和俄罗斯的金融危机使埃及——多亏其国家补贴的银行体系——看似国际投机资金为数不多的避风港之一，但1999年2月之后跌势又起。到次年夏天，市场如此低迷，以至于单只股票——该国新近私有化的手机垄断企业 MobiNil——经常占每日交易量的50%以上，有时高达70%。

en: Most of the remaining stock market activity, and privatization progress, was confined to just one economic sector, construction. The Toshka irrigation scheme and other large government projects, together with the statesubsidized real estate boom and tourism development, provided the only significant source of economic growth. Cement makers, manufacturers of steel reinforcing bars, and contracting companies all prospered, with the contractors’ profit on government projects said to average 30 to 40 percent of income. The demand for cement increased so rapidly that the world’s three largest cement makers, Holderbank of Switzerland, the French-based Lafarge group, and Cemex of Mexico, scrambled to buy up Egypt’s governmentowned cement plants.

The construction boom had turned the country into an importer of cement, so these foreign investments in local cement production should be classified as a return to the unfashionable policies of importsubstitution industrialization. They had nothing to do with the growth of export-oriented industry that the economic reformers had promised.
zh: 其余股市活动和私有化进展大多局限于一个经济部门：建筑业。托什卡灌溉工程和其他大型政府项目，加上国家补贴的房地产繁荣和旅游开发，提供了唯一显著的经济增长来源。水泥生产商、钢筋制造商和承包公司都兴旺发达，据说承包商在政府项目上的利润平均占收入的30%—40%。水泥需求增长如此之快，以致世界三大水泥生产商——瑞士的霍尔班克、总部在法国的拉法基集团和墨西哥的墨西哥水泥公司（Cemex）——争相收购埃及的国有水泥厂。
建筑繁荣使该国成为水泥进口国，因此这些对本地水泥生产的外国投资应归类为回归不时兴的进口替代工业化政策。它们与经济改革者承诺的出口导向型工业增长毫无关系。

en: Real estate booms and stock market swings failed to address the problem of the country’s low levels of domestic investment. Gross domestic investment dropped from 28 percent of GDP in 1980 to 19 percent in 1998, compared to an average of lower and middle income countries of 25 percent.
Between 1990 and 1997 investment grew at only 2.7 percent a year, compared to 7.2 percent for all middle income countries and 12.7 percent for those in East Asia.

In addition, by June 1996 the number of lossmaking public enterprises had almost doubled since the start of the reforms, from fifty-four to one hundred, and accumulated losses had risen from E£2 billion to E£12 billion ($3.5 billion).
The government had redefined its finances to exclude public sector companies from the fiscal accounts, however, so this worsening situation was hidden from view.
The reformers could continue to claim that they were replacing government deficits with a balanced budget.
zh: 房地产繁荣和股市波动未能解决该国国内投资水平低的问题。国内总投资从1980年占GDP的28%降至1998年的19%，而低收入和中等收入国家的平均水平为25%。
1990年至1997年间，投资每年仅增长2.7%，而所有中等收入国家为7.2%，东亚国家为12.7%。
此外，到1996年6月，亏损公共企业的数量自改革开始以来几乎翻倍，从54家增至100家，累计亏损从20亿埃镑增至120亿埃镑（35亿美元）。
然而，政府重新界定了财政，把公共部门公司排除在财政账户之外，因此这一恶化情况被掩藏起来。
改革者可以继续声称，他们正用平衡预算取代政府赤字。

en: The reform program did not remove the state from the market or eliminate profligate public subsidies. Its main impact was to concentrate public funds into different hands, and many fewer. The state turned resources away from agriculture and industry and the underlying problems of training and employment. It now subsidized financiers instead of factories, cement kilns instead of bakeries, speculators instead of schools. Although the IMF showed no interest in examining the question, it was not hard to figure out who was benefiting from the new financial subsidies. The revitalized public-private commercial banks focused their tax-free lending on big loans to large operators. The minimum loan was typically over E£1 million and required large collateral and good connections.
So the subsidized funds were channeled into the hands of a relatively small number of ever more powerful and prosperous financiers and entrepreneurs.
zh: 改革计划没有使国家退出市场，也没有消除挥霍的公共补贴。其主要影响是把公共资金集中到不同的、而且少得多的手中。国家把资源从农业和工业，以及培训与就业等根本问题上转走。它现在补贴的是金融家而非工厂，水泥窑而非面包房，投机者而非学校。尽管IMF对考察这一问题毫无兴趣，但不难看出谁从新的金融补贴中获益。重振的公私合营商业银行把免税贷款集中于向大型经营者提供大额贷款。最低贷款额通常超过100万埃镑，并要求大量抵押品和良好人脉。
因此，补贴资金被输送进相对少数、越来越有权势和财富的金融家和企业家手中。

en: At the top were about two dozen business groups, such as Bahgat, Seoudi, Mohamed Mahmoud, Mansour, Arabian International, Osman, and Orascom. These family-owned enterprise networks typically began as construction companies or import/export agents, which had prospered after 1974 when the government allowed large private entrepreneurs to reemerge following the years of import restrictions and state monopolies. Many depended on lucrative contracts to supply goods and services to the Egyptian military. Most expanded subsequently into tourism, real estate, food and beverages, and computer and internet services, and in some cases the manufacturing of construction materials or, where tariff protection made it profitable, the local assembling of consumer goods such as electronics or cars. Several shared in ownership of the private sector banks, which emerged in the same period. They enjoyed powerful monopolies or oligopolies, in particular as exclusive agents for the goods and services of Western-based transnationals. Nothing one reads in the documents of the IMF or USAID mentions the nature, history, or power of these groups, whose existence was hidden behind the bland formulations of “the private sector” and a revitalized “Egyptian economy.”
zh: 处于顶端的是大约二十几个商业集团，如巴赫加特、塞乌迪、穆罕默德·马哈茂德、曼苏尔、阿拉伯国际、奥斯曼和奥拉斯科姆。这些家族所有的企业网络通常起步于建筑公司或进出口代理商，它们在1974年后繁荣起来，当时政府在多年的进口限制和国家垄断之后允许大型私人企业家重新出现。许多集团依靠向埃及军方供应商品和服务的丰厚合同。多数集团随后扩展到旅游、房地产、食品饮料、计算机和互联网服务，有些还生产建筑材料，或者在关税保护有利可图时，在当地组装电子产品或汽车等消费品。有几家还共同拥有同一时期出现的私营银行。它们享有强大的垄断或寡头地位，尤其是作为西方跨国公司商品和服务的独家代理。在IMF或美国国际开发署的文件中，读不到任何提及这些集团的性质、历史或权力的内容；它们的存在被“私营部门”和重振的“埃及经济”这类平淡表述所掩盖。

en: The Seoudi Group, for example, had its origins in a local trading company set up in 1958 by Abdul Moniem Seoudi. In the mid-1970s, with the opening of the consumer economy, the company began to import foodstuffs, general merchandise, and Suzuki commercial vehicles, and used the new tax-free zones to manufacture and export acrylic yarns. The family was involved in establishing two of the new private sector banks, Al-Mohandes and Watany. In the 1980s they expanded into agribusiness, producing factory chickens and eggs with U.S.-subsidized feed grains and importing American pesticides, feed additives, and agricultural equipment. They also established their own construction company to build facilities for their expanding enterprises. By the 1990s they were assembling Suzuki vehicles and manufacturing car seats and radiators, were the sole importers of Nissan vehicles, and had become the exclusive agents for NCR computers.
zh: 例如，塞乌迪集团起源于阿卜杜勒·穆尼姆·塞乌迪1958年创办的一家本地贸易公司。1970年代中期，随着消费经济开放，该公司开始进口食品、日用百货和铃木商用车，并利用新的免税区生产和出口腈纶纱。家族参与创办了两家新的私营银行——穆汉迪斯银行（Al-Mohandes）和瓦塔尼银行（Watany）。1980年代，他们扩展到农业综合企业，用美国补贴的饲料谷物生产工厂化鸡和鸡蛋，并进口美国农药、饲料添加剂和农业设备。他们还成立了自己的建筑公司，为其扩张的企业建造设施。到1990年代，他们组装铃木汽车，生产汽车座椅和散热器，是日产汽车的唯一进口商，并成为NCR计算机的独家代理。

en: The Metwalli family took control of Arabian International Construction when the company was denationalized in 1987, and built it up as the local partner of transnational firms constructing power stations and other government projects. In the 1990s AIC acquired the local share of two of the largest government contracts, to pipe drinking water under the Suez Canal for the North Sinai Development Project and build the canal and pumping station for the Toshka scheme. The company’s profits on such projects averaged 40 percent of turnover and enabled AIC to become the largest private construction company in Egypt. The income was channeled into eight other family-owned companies, all of them, it was claimed, becoming larger than AIC itself, the largest of them a real estate development company.
zh: 1987年阿拉伯国际建筑公司非国有化时，梅特瓦利家族取得了控制权，并把它发展为承建发电站和其他政府项目的跨国公司的本地合作伙伴。1990年代，AIC获得了两项最大政府合同的本地份额：为北西奈开发项目在苏伊士运河下铺设饮用水管道，以及为托什卡计划修建运河和泵站。公司在此类项目上的利润平均占营业额的40%，使AIC成为埃及最大的私营建筑公司。收入被输送到另外八家家族公司；据称它们都变得比AIC本身更大，其中最大的一家是房地产开发公司。

en: The Mohamed Mahmoud Sons group traced its origins to 1895, when Mohamed Mahmoud inherited his father’s shoe-making workshop, becoming a shoe retailer in the 1920s and by the 1950s the largest shoe manufacturer and exporter in the Middle East. Like other groups, they diversified in the mid-1970s into the wholesale import and distribution of consumer goods, and they became the country’s largest manufacturer of corrugated cardboard boxes. In the 1980s they set up their own engineering and construction arm, and imported and later began to assemble aluminum windows and doors, household and office furniture, and Ukrainianmade tractors and irrigation pipes. By the 1990s the group’s thirteen companies included the MM chain of luxury fashion stores, carrying lines such as Yves Saint Laurent, Church’s, and Fratelli Rossetti; financial interests in the Egyptian Gulf Bank and the Pharaonic Insurance Company; the Datum internet service provider; the sole Egyptian agency for Jaguar Cars; and showrooms selling motor vehicles from Rolls Royce and Ferrari.
zh: 穆罕默德·马哈茂德诸子集团的历史可追溯到1895年，当时穆罕默德·马哈茂德继承了父亲的制鞋作坊，1920年代成为鞋类零售商，到1950年代成为中东最大的制鞋商和出口商。与其他集团一样，他们在1970年代中期实现多元化，进入消费品的批发进口和分销，并成为该国最大的瓦楞纸箱制造商。1980年代，他们建立了自己的工程和建筑部门，进口并后来开始组装铝门窗、家用和办公家具，以及乌克兰制造的拖拉机和灌溉管道。到1990年代，集团的十三家公司包括 MM 高档时装连锁店，经售伊夫·圣罗兰、Church's 和 Fratelli Rossetti 等品牌；在埃及海湾银行和法老保险公司的金融权益；数据网（Datum）互联网服务提供商；捷豹汽车的埃及独家代理；以及出售劳斯莱斯和法拉利汽车的展厅。

en: The Mansour family were large cotton traders whose business was nationalized under President Nasser. In 1975, when private trading companies reemerged, Mansour began importing Chevrolet trucks from General Motors, and later Caterpillar earth-moving equipment and John Deere tractors. A decade later, as the local agents of General Motors, they began assembling Chevrolet and Isuzu commercial vehicles, and by 1993 they controlled 60 percent of the country’s commercial vehicle market, including contracts with the Egyptian military. In the 1990s they acquired the licenses to distribute Marlboro cigarettes and other consumer products, half the Egyptian McDonald’s franchises, and interests in tourism construction and internet technology.
zh: 曼苏尔家族原是大棉花商，其生意在纳赛尔总统时期被国有化。1975年私营贸易公司重新出现时，曼苏尔开始从通用汽车进口雪佛兰卡车，后来进口卡特彼勒土方设备和约翰迪尔拖拉机。十年后，作为通用汽车的本地代理，他们开始组装雪佛兰和五十铃商用车；到1993年，他们控制了该国60%的商用车市场，包括与埃及军方的合同。1990年代，他们取得了万宝路香烟和其他消费品的经销许可、埃及一半的麦当劳特许经营权，以及旅游建筑和互联网技术方面的权益。

en: The Sawiris family worked abroad as contractors in Libya before Sadat’s reopening of business to private entrepreneurs. They returned to make their money as local agents of Hewlett-Packard and AT&T, building U.S.-funded communications networks for the Egyptian military. The profits (30 to 50 percent of turnover was normal, the family claimed) funded an expansion into civilian communications, construction, and tourism. By the 1990s their holding company, Orascom, controlled a dozen subsidiaries that included Egypt’s largest or second largest private construction, cement-making, and natural gas supply companies, the country’s largest tourism developments (funded in part by the World Bank), a military technology import business with offices close to the Pentagon outside Washington, D.C., more than half the local market for Microsoft, Hewlett-Packard, and Lucent Technologies, 60 percent of the country’s internet service provision, and mobile telephone businesses in collaboration with France Télécom controlling a majority of the Egyptian market and taking over local mobile operators in Jordan, Syria, Pakistan, and a dozen countries of sub-Saharan Africa.
zh: 萨维里斯家族在萨达特向私人企业家重新开放商业之前，曾在利比亚做承包商。他们回国后，作为惠普和美国电话电报公司（AT&T）的本地代理赚钱，为埃及军方建设美国资助的通信网络。利润（家族声称通常占营业额的30%—50%）资助了向民用通信、建筑和旅游业的扩张。到1990年代，其控股公司奥拉斯科姆控制着十几家子公司，包括埃及最大或第二大私营建筑、水泥制造和天然气供应公司，该国最大的旅游开发项目（部分由世界银行资助），一家在华盛顿特区郊外五角大楼附近设有办公室的军事技术进口业务，微软、惠普和朗讯科技在当地一半以上的市场，该国60%的互联网服务，以及与法国电信合作、控制埃及市场大部分份额并收购约旦、叙利亚、巴基斯坦和十几个撒哈拉以南非洲国家本地移动运营商的移动电话业务。

en: The Bahgat group, the biggest producer of televisions in the Middle East with a dominant position in the Egyptian market, graduated in the 1990s from assembling Korean sets to making Philips and own-name brands. It was linked to senior military officers and used military-owned factories to build its products. The group’s forty companies (with just three thousand employees) were also involved in assembling electrical appliances and computers, importing medical equipment and irrigation systems, wholesale and retail marketing, tourism development, and computer software and internet service.

They were the builders of the internet-wired Dreamland. Dr. Ahmed Bahgat, the family head, was reputed to be a front man for unpublicized moneymaking by the presidential family, which may explain why the express roads out to Dreamland were built so rapidly.
zh: 巴赫加特集团是中东最大的电视生产商，在埃及市场占据主导地位；它在1990年代从组装韩国电视机升级到生产飞利浦和自有品牌。它与高级军官有联系，并利用军方所有的工厂制造产品。集团的四十家公司（仅有三千名员工）还参与组装电器和计算机，进口医疗设备和灌溉系统，从事批发和零售营销、旅游开发，以及计算机软件和互联网服务。
他们是互联网布线的梦幻乐园的建造者。家族首领艾哈迈德·巴赫加特博士据说是总统家族未公开牟利的代理人，这或许可以解释通往梦幻乐园的快速路为何建得如此之快。

en: Certain common features emerge from these descriptions. Most large business groups were nurtured on government contracts, both civilian and military. Many of these contracts involved projects promoted and supported by USAID. Besides receiving state funds, the business groups relied on close ties with private banks, which were often part of the same family networks. Most avoided the more public method of raising funds on the stock market. The exceptions were those groups that expanded faster than the banks or government could support. The Lakah family, for example, importers of timber and other construction materials since they arrived from Syria in the 1890s, claimed by 1999 to be the largest private business group in Egypt. Rami Lakah had diversified into importing medical equipment and setting up high-tech facilities for the government’s new U.S.- supported “cost-recovery” hospitals for the affluent.

To fund further growth, in August 1999 Lakah had launched the stock market’s largest ever share offer, and in November became the first Egyptian enterprise to borrow on the international bond market. (Disaster, as we will see, was not far ahead.) A final feature these groups shared was the relatively small numbers they employed. With the exception of one or two garment manufacturers, the largest business groups had workforces of only two or three thousand. Most employed considerably fewer.
zh: 从这些描述中可以归纳出某些共同特征。大多数大型商业集团靠民用和军事政府合同滋养壮大。其中许多合同涉及美国国际开发署推动和支持的项目。除了获得国家资金，这些商业集团还依赖与私营银行的密切关系，而私营银行往往属于同一家族网络。多数集团避免采用在股市筹资这种更为公开的方式。例外的是那些扩张速度超过银行或政府支持能力的集团。例如，拉卡家族自1890年代从叙利亚来到这里后一直进口木材和其他建筑材料，到1999年自称是埃及最大的私营商业集团。拉米·拉卡已多元化经营，进口医疗设备，并为政府新设的、由美国支持的面向富人的“成本回收”医院建立高科技设施。
为进一步增长筹资，拉卡于1999年8月发起股市有史以来最大的股票发行，并于11月成为第一家在国际债券市场借款的埃及企业。（正如我们将看到的，灾难已经不远。）这些集团的最后一个共同特征是雇用的员工相对较少。除了一两家服装制造商，最大的商业集团也只有两三千名员工。多数集团雇用的员工要少得多。

en: By the 1990s these enterprises were increasingly concentrating on supplying goods and services affordable to only a small fraction of the population. A “Value Meal” at McDonald’s cost more than the day’s pay of most workers. A family outing to Dreampark, the entertainment complex under construction at Dreamland, would consume a fortnight’s average wages. A pair of children’s shoes at MM’s fashion stores might exceed the monthly pay of a schoolteacher. The Ahram Beverages Company, which produced soft drinks, bottled water, and beer, calculated its potential market (including expatriates and tourists) at just five to six million, in a country of more than sixty million.

This narrow market was the same part of the population that could afford, or could just imagine affording, the country’s 1.3 million private cars—which is why local manufacturers concentrated on assembling Mercedes, BMWs, Jeep Cherokees, and other luxury models.

A company selling upmarket flower bouquets under the U.S. franchise Candy Boutique did its own market research and arrived at a narrower and perhaps more accurate assessment of the affluent: “Egypt has a population of 60 million, but only 20,000 can afford what we are selling.”
Beyond this small group of state-subsidized super-rich, modest affluence probably extended to no more than 5 percent of the population.
zh: 到1990年代，这些企业日益集中于供应只有一小部分人口负担得起的商品和服务。麦当劳的一份“超值套餐”比大多数工人一天的工资还贵。全家去梦幻乐园正在建设的娱乐综合体“梦幻公园”玩一趟，要花掉两周的平均工资。MM时装店的一双童鞋可能超过一名教师一个月的工资。生产软饮料、瓶装水和啤酒的阿赫拉姆饮料公司估计，其潜在市场（包括外派人士和游客）在一个人口超过六千万的国家里只有五六百万人。
这个狭窄的市场，正是有能力——或只能想象有能力——负担该国130万辆私家车的那部分人口；这就是本地制造商集中于组装奔驰、宝马、吉普切诺基和其他豪华车型的原因。
一家以美国特许经营品牌“糖果花店”（Candy Boutique）销售高档花束的公司做了自己的市场调查，得出了对富人更狭窄、或许也更准确的估计：“埃及有六千万人口，但只有两万人买得起我们卖的东西。”
在这个由国家补贴的极小超级富豪群体之外，小康水平的人口大概不超过5%。

en: What of the other 95 percent? Real wages in the public industrial sector dropped by 8 percent from 1990–91 to 1995–96. Other public sector wages remained steady, it was claimed, but could be held up only because the salaries remained below a living wage.

A schoolteacher took home less than $2 a day. One small sign of the times was the reappearance of soup kitchens in Cairo, offering free food to the poor. A more telling sign was that an article in the national press interpreted their appearance not as a mark of how harsh conditions had become but as a welcome return to the kind of private benevolence among the wealthy not seen since the days of the monarchy.
zh: 其余95%的人呢？公共工业部门的实际工资从1990—91年到1995—96年下降了8%。据称其他公共部门的工资保持稳定，但之所以能维持，只是因为薪水仍低于维持生活的工资。
一名教师每天带回家的钱不到2美元。一个微小的时代迹象是开罗重新出现施汤所，向穷人提供免费食物。更能说明问题的是，全国性报纸上的一篇文章把施汤所的出现解释为富人私人慈善的令人欣慰的回归——那种慈善自君主制时代以来就再没见过——而不是解释为生活条件变得多么严酷的标志。

en: Household expenditure surveys showed a sharp decline in real per capita consumption between 1990–91 and 1995–96.The proportion of people below the poverty line increased in this period from about 40 percent (urban and rural) to 45 percent in urban areas and over 50 percent in rural. There was no reliable guide to the changing share of consumption by the very wealthy, because the surveys failed to record most of their spending. If household expenditure surveys for 1991–92 are extrapolated to the national level, the figures show the population as a whole spent E£51 billion. Yet national accounts gave the total expenditure as E£100 billion. In other words, half the country’s consumer spending was missing from the surveys (although this did not deter the World Bank and other agencies from referring to such figures as reasonable indicators of income distribution).

As in India, where a similar disparity was discovered following a decade of economic restructuring, the household surveys probably missed the sharply rising consumption by the very rich, who “downplay their extravagance when the survey people come calling” (or simply have the servants deal with them).

An examination of the kind of expenditures missing from the Egyptian survey and the relative proportion of incomes that different groups spent on food supported the view that the figures underrepresented the concentration of wealth among the rich. Even when categorized quite broadly as those spending more than E£14,000 (about $4,000) a year, wealthy households in Egypt represented only 1.6 million people. One study estimated that this group, less than 3 percent of the population, accounted for half of all consumer spending.
zh: 家庭支出调查显示，1990—91年至1995—96年间实际人均消费急剧下降。这一时期，贫困线以下人口比例从城乡合计约40%上升到城市45%、农村50%以上。对于最富有人群消费份额的变化，没有可靠的指标，因为调查未能记录他们的大部分支出。如果把1991—92年的家庭支出调查外推到全国，数字显示全体人口支出了510亿埃镑。然而国民账户给出的总支出为1000亿埃镑。换言之，全国有一半的消费支出没有出现在调查中（尽管这并未阻止世界银行和其他机构把这些数字称为收入分配的合理指标）。
与印度在经济重组十年后发现类似差距的情况一样，家庭调查可能漏掉了极富者急剧上升的消费，他们“在调查人员上门时轻描淡写自己的奢侈”（或者干脆让仆人去应付）。
对埃及调查所遗漏的支出种类以及不同群体收入中用于食品的相对比例进行考察，支持了这样一种看法：这些数字低估了财富向富人集中的程度。即使把富人宽泛地界定为每年支出超过1.4万埃镑（约4,000美元）者，埃及的富裕家庭也只代表160万人。一项研究估计，这一不足人口3%的群体占全部消费支出的一半。

en: The difficulty of knowing how much of the country’s wealth was becoming concentrated in the hands of the rich was a small part of a larger problem. The politics of economic reform was based upon a fabrication. It depended on the idea that the economy existed as a space that could be surveyed and mapped, much as the Nile valley had been surveyed by Colonel Lyons a century before. It imagined the economy as a territory whose boundaries could be drawn and whose separate elements could be located, transcribed, enumerated, and reorganized. In 1941, when Simon Kuznets of the National Bureau of Economic Research in Cambridge, Massachusetts, first systematized a method for estimating the total size of a nation’s income, he had warned that “a national total facilitates the ascription of independent significance to that vague entity called the national economy.”
Although many economists since Kuznets might have agreed with his warning, the method of their work enabled this vague entity, the economy, to acquire its independence.

The numbers representing national income and output, consumption and savings, employment and productivity, deficits and debt, whatever their degree of reliability, were taken to refer to processes that in principle formed a finite and mappable object.
zh: 难以知道该国多少财富正集中到富人手中，只是一个更大问题的一小部分。经济改革的政策建立在一种虚构之上。它依赖于这样一种观念：经济作为一个空间存在，可以被勘测和绘制，就像一个世纪前莱昂斯上校勘测尼罗河谷那样。它把经济想象成一块疆域，其边界可以划定，其各个要素可以定位、记录、枚举和重新组织。1941年，马萨诸塞州剑桥市国家经济研究局的西蒙·库兹涅茨首次系统提出估算一国收入总额的方法时，就曾警告：“一个全国性总量，便利了人们把独立意义赋予那个被称为国民经济的模糊实体。”
尽管库兹涅茨之后的许多经济学家可能同意他的警告，但他们工作的方法仍使这个模糊实体——经济——获得了独立性。
代表国民收入与产出、消费与储蓄、就业与生产率、赤字与债务的数字，无论其可靠程度如何，都被认为指涉一些原则上构成有限而可测绘对象的过程。

en: Some of the problems with this fabrication are well known. The most frequently mentioned is the impossibility of measuring what is called the informal or parallel sector of the economy. In Egypt the household- or neighborhood-based production and distribution of small-scale goods and services, unregistered with the state and operating on the margins of its systems of revenue and regulation, represents a large but unknown proportion of the country’s productive life.

These activities were traditionally excluded from calculations of GDP and other representations of the economy, although increasing efforts were made to include some estimate. To give one idea of their scale, in 1996 about three-quarters of the population of Greater Cairo was living in informal housing, covering twothirds of the land area and accounting for 85 percent of its dwelling units.

Those living in informal housing were not necessarily employed in informal livelihoods, but the figures indicate the extent to which one sector, the construction and possession of urban housing, was conducted outside the regulation of the state. Estimates of the overall size of informal economic activities ranged from 20 to 35 percent of GDP, but these were guesses and implied a straightforward division between formal and informal that, as we saw with agriculture in the previous chapter, was too simple to capture the interconnections involved.

The economic reforms were aimed chiefly at formal economic activities. As Mahmoud Abdel-Fadil points out, however, policies aimed at the formal sector may have had an opposite impact on the parallel sector, while transformations in the latter, such as those I discussed in agriculture, had a profound effect on the former.
zh: 这种虚构的一些问题众所周知。最常被提到的是无法衡量所谓经济的非正规或平行部门。在埃及，以家庭或邻里为基础的小规模商品和服务生产与分配，未在国家登记，运作于其税收和监管体系的边缘，代表着该国生产生活中很大但未知的一部分。
这些活动传统上被排除在GDP计算和其他经济表述之外，尽管人们日益努力纳入某种估算。为说明其规模：1996年，大开罗约四分之三的人口居住非正规住房，这类住房占土地面积的三分之二，占住房单元的85%。
居住非正规住房的人不一定从事非正规生计，但这些数字表明有一个部门——城市住房的建造和占有——在多大程度上处于国家监管之外。对非正规经济活动总规模的估计在GDP的20%到35%之间，但这些只是猜测，并暗示正规与非正规之间存在一种直接了当的划分；正如我们在上一章农业中看到的，这种划分过于简单，无法把握其中的相互联系。
经济改革主要针对正规经济活动。然而，正如马哈茂德·阿卜杜勒-法迪尔所指出的，针对正规部门的政策可能对平行部门产生相反影响，而平行部门的转变——如我在农业中讨论的那些——又对正规部门产生了深远影响。

en: Not all activities of the parallel sector were small-scale and local. Some played a large role in the country’s international trade and finance, as the example of the hemp industry illustrates. In the 1980s Egypt imported large quantities of processed hemp—cannabis resin— from the Beqaʿa valley in central Lebanon, where civil war had stimulated export-oriented production. The value of Egypt’s clandestine imports was estimated at two to four billion U.S. dollars. Even the lower of these figures exceeded all Egypt’s income from nonpetroleum exports.
After the end of the civil war in 1990, Syria gradually eliminated Lebanese production.

This coincided with currency devaluation in Egypt, which raised import prices, and with declining personal incomes and a tough government campaign against drug importers—conviction for drug dealing now carried the death penalty. As Lebanese hashish became scarce and unaffordable, consumers responded by developing a taste for smoking bango, locally grown, milder, unprocessed cannabis (few regions in the world can produce hemp rich enough in resins to process into hashish).
Hemp production rapidly became a minor village industry, especially in southern Egypt and Sinai, facilitated by the ending of government crop controls.

Thus another import-substitution industry had sprung up, eliminating one of the country’s largest demands for hard currency. None of this was captured in official representations of the Egyptian economy—although the IMF puzzled over an unexplained and unusually rapid decline in the circulation of dollars.
zh: 平行部门的活动并非都是小规模和本地的。正如大麻产业一例所示，有些活动在该国的国际贸易和金融中发挥了重要作用。1980年代，埃及从黎巴嫩中部的贝卡谷地进口大量加工大麻——大麻树脂；该国内战刺激了面向出口的生产。埃及秘密进口的价值估计在20亿至40亿美元之间。即使取较低的数字，也超过了埃及全部非石油出口收入。
1990年内战结束后，叙利亚逐渐铲除了黎巴嫩的生产。
这恰逢埃及货币贬值（抬高了进口价格）、个人收入下降，以及政府对毒品进口商的严厉打击——贩毒定罪现在可判死刑。随着黎巴嫩哈希什变得稀缺且昂贵，消费者的对策是养成了吸食 bango 的口味——本地种植的、较温和的未加工大麻（世界上很少有地区能生产树脂含量足够高、可加工成哈希什的大麻）。
大麻生产迅速成为一项小型乡村产业，尤其是在埃及南部和西奈半岛，政府取消作物控制促进了这一发展。
于是又一个进口替代产业兴起，消除了该国最大的硬通货需求之一。所有这些都没有出现在对埃及经济的官方表述中——尽管IMF曾对美元流通量莫名其妙地异常迅速下降感到困惑。

en: Discussions of the problem of measuring informal and clandestine activities usually imply a contrast with the formal sector, which in comparison is assumed to be fixed and known. Yet with the formal sector too it is difficult to ascribe an “independent significance” to the economy. There can be legal activities whose extent and value is never made public, such as the extensive production, trade, and consumption organized by the Egyptian armed forces. As the U.S. government put it, military spending in Egypt was “not transparent,” so none of this activity was accurately represented in national accounts or in the government budget. In 1989 government spending on the armed forces was estimated at E£4.7 billion, or about 20 percent of government outlays, a figure that excluded foreign military assistance from the United States ($1.3 billion) and Saudi Arabia, income from Egyptian arms exports, and possibly the army’s civilian agriculture and manufacturing projects.

So one-fifth of government spending and perhaps 10 percent of GDP was unmeasured and unreported. In fact the entire government budget was misleading, for in the 1990s Toshka and other giant investment projects were financed without being accounted for in the official figures. The government reported a spending deficit of just 1.3 percent of GDP for 1998–99, but a year later quietly revised this figure to reflect “off-budget spending,” which more than tripled the deficit to 4.3 percent of GDP.
zh: 关于衡量非正规和秘密活动问题的讨论，通常暗示着与正规部门的对照；相比之下，正规部门被假定为固定和已知的。然而，即便在正规部门，也难以把“独立意义”赋予经济。可能存在规模和价值从不公开的合法活动，例如埃及武装部队组织的大规模生产、贸易和消费。用美国政府的说法，埃及的军费开支“不透明”，因此这些活动都没有准确地反映在国民账户或政府预算中。1989年，政府在武装部队上的开支估计为47亿埃镑，约占政府支出的20%；这一数字不包括美国和沙特阿拉伯的对外军事援助（13亿美元）、埃及武器出口收入，以及可能不包括军队的民用农业和制造项目。
因此，五分之一的政府开支和也许10%的GDP未被衡量、未被报告。事实上整个政府预算都具有误导性，因为在1990年代，托什卡和其他巨型投资项目在没有计入官方数字的情况下获得了融资。政府报告1998—99年的支出赤字仅为GDP的1.3%，但一年后悄悄修订这一数字，以反映“预算外支出”，使赤字增加两倍多，达到GDP的4.3%。

en: The problems of informal, clandestine, and unreported economic activities are so great that these alone would provide sufficient reason to question the idea that the economy is an object that can be mapped and measured. But these issues are not the real problem. The idea of the economy presents a larger difficulty. Even the most visible and regulated acts of economic exchange have effects that escape observation or measurement. In any economic transaction the parties involved attempt to calculate, as best they can, what they will gain from the exchange and what it will cost them. The transaction will also affect others, however, either positively or negatively. These further costs and gains will not enter into the calculation, because those affected are not parties to the transaction. Since the size of the economy is measured as the aggregate of all individual transactions, the additional effects are excluded from the representation of the national economy. Economists call the excluded elements “externalities,” and often give the example of pollution: the owners of a cement factory contract with a customer to supply so many tons of cement, and do not include in the price the cost of the air pollution the factory creates, because those living nearby who are harmed by the bad air are not parties to the exchange. In the language of neoclassical economics, externalities are an example of “market failure,” situations where the price mechanism that governs exchanges fails to reflect the true costs involved, and therefore is unable to act as an efficient regulator of social action.
zh: 非正规、秘密和未报告的经济活动问题如此严重，仅这些问题就足以让人质疑经济是一个可以测绘和衡量的对象的观念。但这些并不是真正的问题。经济的观念带来了更大的困难。即使最显眼、最受监管的经济交换行为，也会产生逃逸观察或衡量的效果。在任何经济交易中，当事各方都尽力计算他们将从交换中获得什么、付出什么。然而，交易也会影响其他人，或有利或有害。这些进一步的费用和收益不会进入计算，因为受影响者不是交易方。由于经济规模是以所有个人交易的加总来衡量的，这些额外效果被排除在国民经济表述之外。经济学家把被排除的要素称为“外部性”，并常以污染为例：水泥厂所有者与客户订约供应若干吨水泥，却不把工厂造成的空气污染成本计入价格，因为住在附近、受污浊空气之害的人不是交易方。用新古典经济学的语言说，外部性是“市场失灵”的一个例子，即支配交换的价格机制未能反映所涉真实成本，因而无法充当社会行动的有效调节者。

en: By using examples such as pollution, and by labeling them as externalities or failures, the method and language of economics treat these uncounted costs as something residual. They represent an imperfection in the market, a lapse in its mechanisms, a secondary rather than essential aspect of its operation. The example of pollution inadvertently points to much larger externalities, however, such as the destructive impact of a general level of economic activity on the ecological balance. These represent not individual market failures but an inability of the principle of the market to account for complex effects whose value cannot be monetarized. But in addition to these wider issues, there is a more general problem with treating externalities as something exceptional. Since no transaction takes place in a vacuum, all acts of exchange produce externalities. Every purchase of an object or service involves all the costs that went into it that were excluded, or not properly recognized or compensated.
zh: 通过使用污染之类例子，并给它们贴上外部性或失灵的标签，经济学的方法和语言把这些未计入的成本当作某种残余之物。它们代表市场的不完美、其机制的失效，是其运行中次要而非本质的方面。然而，污染的例子无意中指向远更大的外部性，例如总体经济活动水平对生态平衡的破坏性影响。这些不是个别的市场失灵，而是市场原则无力计入价值无法货币化的复杂效果。但除了这些更广泛的问题外，把外部性当作例外之物还有一个更普遍的问题。由于没有交易发生在真空中，所有交换行为都产生外部性。每一次购买物品或服务，都涉及其中被排除、未被适当承认或补偿的全部成本。

en: It is not surprising that an economic actor should want to acquire something without paying all the associated costs—without accounting for all the ways its production and consumption might affect others. On the contrary, exchange would be impossible if people were made to account for every cost. A market economy requires conventions and powers that enable the completion of an exchange without satisfying such a standard. So when the calculation of the economy excludes not only much that is informal or clandestine, but also the “external” aspects that occur within what is considered formal and regulated, the exclusion is not exceptional or secondary in significance. As Callon points out, a lot of work and expense goes into achieving these acts of exclusion.

Without them, in fact, the market would cease to function. For example, to sell the cement a factory produces the management of the factory must prove they own the product. They must deny the claims of others who may demand some share, such as the kiln workers who produced the cement but may not have been fully compensated for the value contributed by their labor, or those who supplied the machinery or the raw materials, as well as those who demand compensation for the damage pollution has done to their health and other outsiders. By proving ownership the managers exercise a form of exclusion, the power to deny the claims of others.
zh: 经济行为者想要获得某物而不支付全部相关成本——不计入其生产和消费可能影响他人的所有方式——并不令人惊讶。相反，如果人们被迫计入每一项成本，交换就不可能进行。市场经济需要一些惯例和权力，使交换得以在不满足这种标准的情况下完成。因此，当经济的计算不仅排除许多非正规或秘密的东西，还排除被视为正规和受监管范围内发生的“外部”方面时，这种排除并非例外，也不是次要的。正如卡隆所指出的，实现这些排除行为需要大量工作和费用。
事实上，没有它们，市场就会停止运转。例如，要出售工厂生产的水泥，工厂管理层必须证明他们拥有该产品。他们必须否认其他可能要求分得一杯羹者的主张，例如生产水泥、其劳动所创造的价值可能未获充分补偿的窑工，提供机器或原材料的人，以及要求赔偿污染对其健康造成损害的人和其他外部人。通过证明所有权，管理者行使了一种排除形式，即否认他人主张的权力。

en: In chapter 2 I examined the genealogy of one kind of ownership claim in Egypt, the private ownership of land. I traced the process by which a person called the “landowner” came to monopolize the rights to the produce of the land and exclude the entitlements that cultivators, the indigent, the ruling household in Cairo, and other claimants had previously enjoyed. Organizing these exclusions was a complex political project, requiring a variety of forms of violence, supervision, policing, military occupation, legal argument, imprisonment, and economic theory. As that example showed, property is not a simple arrangement, nor a static one. In the twentieth century the cultivators managed to reestablish some of their claims, as did the government. Toward the end of the century, as we saw in chapter 8, reasserting the prerogatives of private ownership required new rounds of violence, policing, and economic argument.
zh: 在第2章中，我考察了埃及一种所有权主张的谱系，即土地私有制。我追溯了被称为“地主”的人如何逐步垄断土地产出的权利，并排除耕种者、穷人、开罗的统治家族以及其他主张者先前享有的权益。组织这些排除是一项复杂的政治工程，需要各种形式的暴力、监督、治安、军事占领、法律论证、监禁和经济理论。正如那个例子所表明的，财产不是一种简单的安排，也不是静止不变的。在20世纪，耕种者设法重新确立了他们的一些主张，政府也是如此。到该世纪之末，正如我们在第8章所见，重新主张私有制的特权需要新一轮的暴力、治安和经济论证。

en: Thus the simple idea of “externality” rests upon the operation of complex and mobile forms of law, international convention, government, corporate power, and economics. These multiple arrangements make possible the economy. Property rights, tax rules, contract and criminal law, administrative regulation, and policing all contribute to fixing the difference between the formal and the informal, between the act of exchange and its externalities, between those with rights and those without, between measurable values and the unmeasurable. In economic theory many of these forms of regulation and enforcement are called institutions. A distinction is sometimes made between formal institutions, such as laws and administrative rules, and informal institutions, such as codes of conduct, implicit understandings, and norms of social action. Institutional economics understands these rules and norms as constraints that organize and set limits to human action.

Like the concept of externality, the term “constraint” characterizes these arrangements once again as secondary, as something outside the economic process itself. The economic act is by definition the expression of an individual choice, the fulfillment of a desire, just as the economy is the sum total of these economic choices and their fulfillment. The desire is the starting point of the economic, while institutions are understood as arrangements that limit the desire, restrict the ways in which needs can be satisfied, prevent others from disrupting their satisfaction, and reduce delinquency or misunderstanding. Constraint is the opposite of desire, an element of incompatibility, and can combine with it only as something external and subordinate. Yet these secondary, external, residual arrangements at the same time are something prior. The rules, norms, and unwritten understandings must exist before the act of exchange, otherwise they could not regulate it.

They are also ubiquitous, dwelling surreptitiously within every economic act. So although economics must portray them as external, secondary, and residual, they are also the condition of possibility of the economic.
zh: 因此，“外部性”这个简单观念依赖于法律、国际公约、政府、公司权力和经济学的复杂而流动的形式的运作。这些多重安排使经济成为可能。财产权、税收规则、合同法和刑法、行政监管和治安，都有助于确定正规与非正规、交换行为与其外部性、有权利者与无权利者、可衡量价值与不可衡量价值之间的差别。在经济理论中，许多这类监管和执行形式被称为制度。人们有时区分正式制度（如法律和行政规则）与非正式制度（如行为准则、默契理解和社会行动规范）。制度经济学把这些规则和规范理解为组织并限制人类行动的约束。

与外部性概念一样，“约束”一词再次把这些安排描述为次要的、处于经济过程本身之外的东西。经济行为按定义是个体选择的表达、欲望的满足，正如经济是这些经济选择及其满足的总和。欲望是经济的起点，而制度被理解为限制欲望、限定需求满足方式、防止他人干扰满足、减少违约或误解的安排。约束是欲望的对立面，是不相容的要素，只能作为外在和从属的东西与之结合。然而这些次要的、外在的、残余的安排同时又是某种在先的东西。规则、规范和不成文理解必须在交换行为之前存在，否则就无法调节它。
它们也无处不在，潜藏在每一个经济行为之中。因此，尽管经济学必须把它们描绘为外在、次要和残余的，它们同时又是经济之所以可能的条件。

en: The constraints, understandings, and powers that frame the economic act, and the economy as a whole, and thus make the economy possible, at the same time render it incomplete. They occur as that strange phenomenon, the constitutive outside.

They are an interior-exterior, something both marginal and central, simultaneously the condition of possibility of the economy and the condition of its impossibility. Callon describes what he calls the “dual nature” of these constraints or frames.

Their purpose is to exclude, to keep out of the picture all those claims, costs, interruptions, and misunderstandings that would make the act of exchange, and thus the economy itself, impossible to complete. To achieve this “enframing,” the rules, procedures, institutions, and methods of enforcement are thought to have a special status.

Just as a frame seems distinct from the picture it enframes, and a rule is supposedly an abstraction in relation to the concrete actions it governs, the institutions that enframe the economy are imagined to have a different, and extraeconomic, nature. They are the arena of economic actions, as distinct from the actions themselves. In practice, however, this distinction is not a stable one. Each piece of the frame, each rule, procedure, understanding, constraint, enforcement, and sanction, involves potential exchanges of its own. To apply a rule, for example, one must negotiate its limits and exceptions, since no rule contains its own interpretation. These negotiations become part of the act of exchange they are supposed to regulate. To act according to an implicit understanding, or an accepted norm, one must engage over time in a series of exchanges, economic and noneconomic, out of which the norm or understanding emerges. To enforce a regulation involves all the expense and interactions of adjudication, resort to force, and monitoring. At every one of these points the “frame” opens up and reveals its dual nature. Instead of acting as a limit, containing the economic, it becomes a series of exchanges and connections that involve the act of exchange in a potentially limitless series of further interactions.

Thus the problem of fixing the economy is not a residual one of accounting for informal and clandestine activities, or turning externalities into internal costs. The problem is that the frame or border of the economy is not a line on a map, but a horizon that at every point opens up into other territories.
zh: 为经济行为乃至整个经济设定框架、从而使经济成为可能的约束、理解和权力，同时也使经济不完整。它们以那种奇怪的现象出现，即构成性外部。
它们是内部-外部，既边缘又核心，同时是经济可能性的条件和经济不可能性的条件。卡隆描述了这些约束或框架的“双重性质”。
它们的目的是排除，把所有会使交换行为——从而经济本身——无法完成的主张、成本、干扰和误解挡在画面之外。为实现这种“框架化”，规则、程序、制度以及执行方法被认为具有特殊地位。

正如画框似乎不同于它所框定的图画，规则据称是相对于其支配的具体行动的抽象，为经济设定框架的制度被想象为具有不同的、经济之外的性质。它们是经济行动的舞台，不同于行动本身。然而在实践中，这种区分并不稳定。框架的每一部分、每一条规则、程序、理解、约束、执行和制裁，都涉及自身的潜在交换。例如，要适用一条规则，就必须协商其界限和例外，因为没有一条规则包含自身的解释。这些协商成为它们本应调节的交换行为的一部分。要依照默契理解或公认规范行事，人们必须长期参与一系列经济和非经济的交换，规范或理解正是从中产生的。执行一项法规涉及裁决、诉诸武力和监督的全部费用与互动。在每一个这样的点上，“框架”都会打开，显露出其双重性质。它不再充当限制、包容经济，而变成一系列交换和联系，使交换行为卷入一个潜在无限的进一步互动序列。
因此，确定经济的问题不是一个残余问题——不是核算非正规和秘密活动，也不是把外部性转化为内部成本。问题在于，经济的框架或边界不是地图上的一条线，而是一条地平线，在每一点上都展开为其他疆域。

en: There are three issues to elaborate before we return to the question of the relationship between economics and the economy. First, the rules of the market are by no means the only kind of frame for economic transactions. Despite the importance given to laws of property and the principles of the price mechanism, it would be difficult to establish that the market is even the most significant arena of exchange. Many other forms of social practice structure the way transactions occur, often with the purpose of preventing them from leaking across into the market. One institution that has always offered alternative rules and powers to those of property and contract is the household or family. We have seen how in Egypt, as in many parts of the world, the new large-scale economic activities that flourished with free-market reforms operated through networks of family-held businesses. Here the main economic institution was not the market or even the business enterprise, but a web of personal ties drawing together a series of businesses, often establishing connections within and across state institutions, the banking sector, the armed forces, or the local agencies of transnational corporations. These networks operate through relations of kinship or marriage and put to work all the powers of loyalty, affection, discipline, and compulsion on which such relations depend.
zh: 在回到经济学与经济之间关系的问题之前，还有三个问题需要详述。第一，市场规则绝不是经济交易的唯一框架。尽管财产法和价格机制原则备受重视，却很难证明市场甚至是最重要的交换场所。许多其他形式的社会实践塑造着交易发生的方式，其目的常常是防止交易渗漏到市场中。一向提供不同于财产和合同规则与权力的制度，就是家户或家庭。我们已看到，在埃及如同世界许多地方，随自由市场改革而繁荣的新的大型经济活动，是如何通过家族企业网络运作的。这里主要的经济制度不是市场，甚至不是企业，而是一张把一系列企业拉在一起的人际关系网，常常在国家机构、银行部门、武装力量或跨国公司本地代理机构内部和之间建立联系。这些网络通过亲属或婚姻关系运作，调动起此类关系所依赖的忠诚、情感、纪律和强制等全部力量。

en: These powers, like so many other noncapitalist forces operating at the center of so-called capitalism, need constant attention. They are never entirely controlled by those who use them and can easily take their own course. Trouble can follow, for example, when the forces of affection or ties of matrimony break down. The rupture can cause mundane economic difficulties, or can lead to major crises. In 1995 the entire Egyptian banking and political system was shaken by the rupturing of one family network. The Ayuti family controlled, among other interests, one of Egypt’s large private sector financial houses, Nile Bank. ʿIsa al-Ayuti, the eighty-oneyear-old chairman of the bank, had become estranged from his daughter ʿAliya al-Ayuti, the bank’s managing director, following her marriage to Mahmud ʿAzzam, a large contractor and a member of parliament. In December 1995 the father accused his daughter of making unsecured loans to her new husband, providing his construction company with almost E£80 million. A government investigation of the fraud later widened to include thirty-two bankers and entrepreneurs involved in E£1 billion in fraudulent deals, including a former minister of tourism, Tawfiq ʿAbdu Ismaʿil, who was chairman of Dakhiliya Bank and also an MP, and two other members of parliament.

This was one of a number of fraud cases in this period arising from the breakdown of family networks. What such incidents reveal is not that all family networks involve fraud. Rather, the sensational cases publicized in the media indicate the quieter, everyday work that must be done to maintain family networks, and the costs that can follow from their collapse. Once again, the borders of the economic do not occur as a simple constraint or frame, but open up into further territories, draw upon further forces, and channel other powers and desires.
zh: 这些力量，如同在所谓资本主义中心运作的许多其他非资本主义力量一样，需要持续关注。它们从未被使用者完全控制，很容易自行其是。例如，当情感力量或婚姻纽带破裂时，麻烦便随之而来。断裂可能造成日常经济困难，也可能导致重大危机。1995年，一个家族网络的破裂震动了整个埃及银行和政治体系。阿尤提家族控制着埃及一家大型私营金融机构尼罗河银行及其他权益。银行八十一岁的董事长伊萨·阿尤提与女儿、银行总经理阿利娅·阿尤提关系疏远，因为女儿嫁给了大承包商、议员马哈茂德·阿扎姆。1995年12月，父亲指控女儿向新婚丈夫发放无担保贷款，为其建筑公司提供了近8000万埃镑。政府对这起欺诈案的调查后来扩大到32名银行家和企业家，涉及10亿埃镑的欺诈交易，包括前旅游部长陶菲克·阿卜杜·伊斯梅尔（他是内政银行董事长，也是议员）和另外两名议员。
这是这一时期因家族网络破裂而产生的若干欺诈案之一。这类事件所揭示的并不是所有家族网络都涉及欺诈。相反，媒体大肆宣传的耸动案件，恰恰表明维持家族网络必须做那些较为安静的日常工作，以及网络崩溃可能带来的代价。经济边界再次不是作为简单的约束或框架出现，而是展开为更多疆域，汲取更多力量，疏导其他权力和欲望。

en: Another well-known example of a large-scale nonmarket economic network is the transnational corporation—an institution whose history and power must be discussed in relation to a parallel mechanism for limiting the operation of the market, the nation-state. Of course we know from Marx that any capitalist enterprise is a means of employing nonmarket arrangements to produce goods or services for the market. While the owners of the enterprise sell its products on the market, those who are employed to produce the products are typically subject to multiple forms of discipline, surveillance, compulsion, and, in many cases, the threat or use of violence. The fact that the employment relation takes the outward form of a contract only thinly disguises the “dull compulsion of economic relations,” as Marx described it in volume one of Capital, that gives most employees—especially those outside the more privileged economic enclaves of the West—little room to bargain over the terms of their labor.

The large corporation, however, develops nonmarket arrangements to a much further extent. It establishes extensive hierarchies and controls based on supervision, surveillance, rules, sanctions, and the manufacture of a corporate culture. It separates the management of economic processes from the old powers of ownership. And it organizes multiple transactions within the corporation itself, producing, distributing, and consuming goods and services among its various divisions and subsidiaries. Indeed the closely governed, nonmarket movement of goods and services within corporate hierarchies represents as much as one-third of international trade.
zh: 另一个众所周知的大规模非市场经济网络例子是跨国公司——讨论它的历史和权力，必须联系到限制市场运作的平行机制：民族国家。当然，我们从马克思那里知道，任何资本主义企业都是利用非市场安排为市场生产商品或服务的手段。企业所有者在市场上出售产品，而受雇生产产品的人通常受制于多种纪律、监视、强制，以及在许多情况下的暴力威胁或使用。雇佣关系表面上采取合同形式，这一点只是薄薄地掩盖了马克思在《资本论》第一卷中所描述的“经济关系的无声强制”；这种强制使大多数雇员——尤其是西方较特权经济飞地之外的人——几乎没有就劳动条件讨价还价的余地。
然而，大公司把非市场安排发展到了远为深入的程度。它建立起基于监督、监视、规则、制裁和企业文化营造的广泛等级和控制。它把经济过程的管理与旧的所有权权力分开。它在公司内部组织多重交易，在各分支机构和子公司之间生产、分配和消费商品与服务。事实上，公司等级体系内部受到严格治理的商品和服务非市场流动，占国际贸易的三分之一之多。

en: By the time he drafted volume three of Capital, Marx was aware that the modern corporation represented a break with the principles of capitalism he had outlined in volume one. He described the joint-stock company as “the abolition of the capitalist mode of production within the capitalist mode of production itself.”
